source_text: From a medical perspective, clitoridectomy, classified as Type I female genital mutilation (FGM) involving partial or total removal of the clitoral prepuce and/or glans, carries significant immediate risks including severe pain, hemorrhage, infection, urinary retention, and tetanus, with mortality rates reported up to 1-2% in some non-sterile settings due to sepsis or shock. [1] [6]
